name: Evaluation and Reconstruction Metrics
text:
# Evaluation and Reconstruction Metrics
Also called: Evaluation Methodology for SLF
## Overview
This family provides metrics and objectives to evaluate the quality, stability, and robustness of [radiance field optimizations](#44-radiance-field-optimization.md) and volume renderings, distinct from the [regularization losses](#1413-regularization-losses.md) that drive optimization [G]. Unlike sibling methods that enforce smoothness or perceptual similarity, such as [Total Variation Regularization](860-total-variation-regularization.md) or [Perceptual Loss Training](2000-perceptual-loss-training.md), these metrics serve as diagnostic tools or final benchmarks to assess specific failure modes such as flickering, geometric inconsistency across views, or adversarial sensitivity [G].
## Shared principles

## Subtopics

### [Temporal Instability Metric](1921-temporal-instability-metric.md)
Quantifies temporal coherence by measuring frame-to-frame variations in reconstruction error. Lower values indicate smoother temporal consistency. Sets it apart: focuses on video/flicker artifacts rather than static image quality. Choose when evaluating temporal stability in novel view synthesis sequences.

### [Inverse Mean Residual Color (IMRC) Metric](10556-inverse-mean-residual-color-imrc-metric.md)
Evaluates geometric quality without ground-truth geometry by measuring transmittance-density-weighted residual color in decibels. Sets it apart: evaluates the entire density field rather than a single iso-surface. Choose when assessing geometry consistency without ground-truth meshes.

### [Across View-direction Inconsistency (AVI) Metric](11106-across-view-direction-inconsistency-avi-metric.md)
Quantifies geometrical inconsistency between adjacent viewing directions by leveraging ground truth optical flow to warp views. Sets it apart: targets 3D geometry consistency across viewpoints rather than temporal or static quality. Choose when evaluating spatial coherence in volumetric super-resolution.

### [Ray Diversity Objective](13003-ray-diversity-objective.md)
Quantifies ray variation from various poses observing a mesh face. Sets it apart: combines geometric diversity with a quality penalty to guide active view planning. Choose when optimizing camera poses for reconstruction.

### [Adversarial Robustness Evaluation](16421-adversarial-robustness-evaluation.md)
Assesses stability under small input perturbations by computing the [BREN](#16414-bounded-relative-error-norm-bren.md) ratio. Sets it apart: evaluates sensitivity to artifacts from targeted input noise rather than reconstruction error. Choose when testing network robustness against adversarial attacks.

### [Ambiguity-Aware Inverse Rendering Evaluation Metrics](19381-ambiguity-aware-inverse-rendering-evaluation-metrics.md)
Quantifies uncertainty by measuring variance across stochastic samples. Sets it apart: evaluates stability under varying conditions and solution diversity in ill-posed inverse problems. Choose when assessing albedo/illumination estimates in ambiguous scenarios.

### [Registration Metric Evaluation Protocol](21625-registration-metric-evaluation-protocol.md)
Optimization-independent method evaluating [rigid registration](#21006-rigid-registration-via-mutual-information-maximization.md) similarity by sampling the parameter space around a golden standard. Sets it apart: provides statistical characterizations of the metric's landscape decoupled from algorithm convergence. Choose when benchmarking registration similarity measures.

### [Reconstruction Error (RE) Metric](21653-reconstruction-error-re-metric.md)
Quantifies pixel-wise discrepancy using the L2 norm. Sets it apart: provides a direct, global measure of photometric fidelity between synthesized and observed input. Choose when requiring a standard baseline for photometric accuracy.

### Leak Metric
Measures the fraction of a method's near-plane foreground energy that incorrectly falls on the culled side where the reference is background [S2, unofficial]. Combines proxy reconstruction error, renderer mismatch, soft tails, and overshooting culls [S2, unofficial]. Steps: 1. Compute method foreground mask $F(R)$ using $\theta_{fg} = 0.04$ [S2, unofficial]. 2. Define near-plane region $N$ as pixels in $F(R)$ with $|s| \leq 60$ [S2, unofficial]. 3. Define leak region $L$ as pixels in $N$ with $s > 2$ that are not in reference foreground $F(G)$ [S2, unofficial]. 4. Sum $\max_c R_c(\mathbf{x})$ over $L$ and $N$ across all grazing views, then take ratio [S2, unofficial]. Formula: $N = F(R) \cap \{|s| \leq 60\}$, $L = N \cap \{s > 2\} \setminus F(G)$. $\text{Leak} = \frac{\sum_{\mathbf{x} \in \mathcal{L}} \max_{\mathbf{x}} R_c(\mathbf{x})}{\sum_{\mathbf{x} \in \mathcal{N}} \max_{\mathbf{x}} R_c(\mathbf{x})}$ [S2, unofficial]. Parameters: Foreground threshold $\theta_{fg} = 0.04$. Cut-edge margin $\delta = 2$ (for $s > 2$). Near-plane half-width $w = 60$ (for $|s| \leq 60$) [S2, unofficial]. Pitfalls: Averaging per-view ratios on thin grazing bands causes numerical instability. Pooling sums across all views before taking the ratio stabilizes the metric [S2, unofficial].

### Band Fidelity Metric (Sb)
A fidelity metric measuring the structural similarity between a method's render and a reference render over the exposed cut face (reference foreground) [S2, unofficial]. Steps: Compute scalar luminance $Y(x) = \frac{1}{3} \sum_c I_c(x) \in [0, 1]$ at each pixel $x$. Compute foreground mask $F(I) = \{x : \max_c I_c(x) > \theta_{fg}\}$ with $\theta_{fg} = 0.04$ [S2, unofficial]. Compute SSIM between method render and reference restricted to $F(G)$ [S2, unofficial]. Average the SSIM values across all perpendicular views of all planes in the evaluated set [S2, unofficial]. Parameters: Foreground threshold $\theta_{fg} = 0.04$. Band $\mathcal{B}$ for $S_b$ is the reference foreground $F(G)$ [S2, unofficial]. Pitfalls: Band PSNR is omitted from main tables because operator differences are only hundredths of a decibel and leakage can offset small brightness bias [S2, unofficial].

### Model Validation using RMSE and EMD
A validation procedure assessing model generalization on a hold-out set of 2,000 volume-rendered images not used for training [S3]. EMD (Earth Mover’s Distance) is used to measure higher-level similarity between color histograms, mitigating misalignment in histogram space [S3]. Parameters: RMSE (Root [Mean Squared Error](#1651-mse-loss-and-psnr-conversion.md)) is used as the primary evaluation metric for image similarity [S3]. EMD Cost Normalization: The cost between histogram bins is normalized such that the maximum cost is 1 [S3]. Numbers: Training Time: 16.5 hours. Rendering Time: 0.007 seconds per image. TF Exploration Time: 0.06 seconds. TF Sensitivity Time: 0.49 seconds [S3].

### Baseline Calibration
A calibration procedure that drives a scene reconstruction as close as possible to ground truth in image space without using network losses, to establish a threshold for metamerism [S4, unofficial]. Steps: For shape reconstruction, use mean-absolute error between rendered and ground-truth views. For material reconstruction, use the Dual-Buffer loss to handle Monte Carlo noise from path tracing [S4, unofficial]. Compute the baseline score using the network's latent space projection on masked images [S4, unofficial]. Formula: $\text{score}_{\text{baseline}} = \text{score}(\text{NN}(m(n) \odot \hat{x}(n)), \text{NN}(m(n) \odot x_i(n)))$ [S4, unofficial]. Parameters: $m(n)$: A binary foreground mask that suppresses background regions [S4, unofficial]. Pitfalls: Do not mask material experiments because the object's appearance depends on global illumination and indirect lighting; masking would discard appearance cues [S4, unofficial].

## Background
Specialized metrics have been developed to address specific artifacts and evaluation needs, such as temporal instability in novel view synthesis [G], geometric consistency across views [G], and geometry evaluation without ground-truth meshes [G]. The family also includes specialized metrics for evaluating [clipping](#1444-clipping.md) and cutting operations in medical volume rendering, such as Leak and Band Fidelity, which address artifacts specific to half-space clipping techniques [S2, unofficial].
